items.fullSpeechOutput: Adverbial placement with clause boundaries. Which option correctly joins a fronted adverbial to a main clause AND uses the right boundary punctuation? before the bell rang / the children lined up quietly. Choose one. Options: Before the bell rang; the children lined up quietly.. Before the bell rang the children lined up quietly.. Before the bell rang, the children lined up quietly.. Before, the bell rang the children lined up quietly.
_solutionLines: This question tests adverbials and clauses and boundary punctuation together.
A fronted adverbial clause needs a comma after it to mark the boundary between the adverbial and the main clause. A semicolon is wrong because the adverbial is not an independent clause.
The correct option is: Before the bell rang, the children lined up quietly.
